source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), section 5.2
text:
Consistency in quality grading matters as much to Chinese buyers as the quality level itself: a supplier whose fruit quality varies unpredictably between shipments is seen as a bigger risk than one whose fruit is reliably mid-grade, because unpredictability makes it hard for a buyer to plan resale or maintain their own reputation downstream. The guide stresses matching grading practice to the specific standard the buyer expects (size, appearance, ripeness stage at shipping), maintaining that standard shipment after shipment, and keeping records that support traceability back to which orchard and packing run produced a given batch.

Poor or inconsistent quality control at this stage is described as directly damaging an exporter's reputation and future sales prospects with Chinese buyers, since a single bad shipment can outweigh several good ones in a buyer's overall assessment of a supplier's reliability.
